title: Latency-fidelity sampling journal — Arjun
content:
Goal:
Quick exploration of how aggressive sampling (high temp / high top_p) interacts with 8-bit quantization and asymmetric warmup priming. Trying to capture signal for tail-latency regressions that only show up for low-probability token paths.

Notes / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis A: High-temp sampling increases per-token CPU time (softmax + multinomial) and produces more KV cache churn when repeated tokens are less predictable — amplifies p95/p99.
- Hypothesis B: 8-bit quant reduces arithmetic precision and might increase variance of long-token-generation branches, showing up as rare spikes.
- Hypothesis C: Short prefix warmup (1-2 tokens) vs long prefix warmup (32 tokens) causes asymmetric cache priming; some attention kernels behave differently causing small cold-starts mid-request.

Experiment setup:
- Model: llama-2-13b-chat (hf checkpoint converted) — serving variant used for internal perf rigs (config: sequence_len=2048, kv_cache enabled).
- Quantization: baseline FP16 vs dynamic-quant 8-bit (perf path) — run both on same node to compare.
- Hardware: single A100-40GB (node id gpu-3), 1x worker, BFC allocator, CUDA kernels with cuBLAS fused attention.
- Client: grpc multi-stream harness, synthetic prompt generator (zipfian token lengths), sustained QPS 15 -> 60 ramp.
- Sampling params tested: (temp, top_p, top_k) pairs: 
   A: (0.2, 0.9, 40)  -- conservative
   B: (0.8, 0.95, 200) -- exploratory/high-entropy
   C: (1.2, 1.0, 0)   -- near pure sampling
- Prefix warmup lengths: 2, 8, 32 tokens (to test asymmetric priming)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for first token and steady-state token, kv_cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, CPU softmax time (measured via microprofiler).

Quick raw observations (novice-run, noisy):
- FP16, conservative sampling (A), warmup=32: p50=34ms, p95=160ms, p99=410ms (steady-state token).
- FP16, exploratory sampling (B), warmup=2: p50=48ms, p95=320ms, p99=980ms. Noticeable long tails on p99.
- 8-bit, sampling B, warmup=2: p50=52ms, p95=470ms, p99=1.6s. 8-bit amplified spikes (p95->p99 gap widens).
- 8-bit, sampling C (temp=1.2), warmup=32: unexpectedly lower p50 (cache priming reduced some kernel overhead) but p99 remained >1.7s on some runs.

ASCII micro-table (steady-state token p95/p99):
- FP16 A (32): p95 160ms | p99 410ms
- FP16 B (2):  p95 320ms | p99 980ms
- Q8    B (2):  p95 470ms | p99 1600ms
- Q8    C (32): p95 380ms | p99 1720ms

Interpretation / thoughts:
- Sampling entropy clearly dominates tail behavior. Large top_k / top_p expands softmax work and sampling branches; this increases CPU/GPU coordination cost (kernel launch, memory traffic).
- Quantization (dynamic 8-bit) doesn't just change mean latency — it increases variance. Suspect that reduced precision causes occasional slower attention execution paths (fallbacks or additional correction steps in kernels). Need to inspect kernel logs for "recompute" or fallback.
- Warmup helps reduce some overhead (especially when long prefix primes KV cache), but it doesn't eliminate high-entropy-induced tails. Warmup=32 lowered p95 for Q8 in one config, but p99 stayed high.

Anomalies to investigate:
- Several p99 spikes coincided with short-lived GPU SM utilization drops (~200ms) while CPU softmax time spiked. Could be host->device synchronization or an unexpected memcpy triggered by certain sampling shapes.
- One run logged: "attention_kernel_fallback=true" in debug trace during Q8 B (2) experiments — investigate kernel's fallback triggers.

Mini checklist / next steps:
- [ ] Re-run targeted micro-benchmark with profiler ON for p99 windows (nsys/torch profiler) to capture kernel stacks for the slow tokens.
- [ ] Add counters to detect kernel fallbacks / reorders in runtime (instrument attention path).
- [ ] Compare with an alternative sampling implementation (vectorized multinomial vs per-token loop) to isolate CPU-side sampling cost.
- [ ] Test 4-bit quant (if available) with the same sampling params to see monotonicity of variance.
- [ ] Add synthetic worst-case prompts that encourage rare tokens (math expressions / low-frequency tokens) to stress tails.

Quick hypothesis to test first: spikes are multi-factor — high entropy -> irregular output length + quantization-induced kernel fallback -> host sync -> p99 spike. If true, mitigating could be: (a) batch sampling operations (vectorize), (b) add small async prefetch for memcopies, (c) guard quant kernels to avoid occasional fallback by relaxing quant thresholds.

Random notes / logs:
- Debug run id: run-2024-11-07T18:12:03Z (attached nsys trace saved under experiment-traces/run-07.tgz)
- Observed KV hit ratio ~0.94 for long-prefix runs, ~0.71 for short-prefix runs.

If anyone picks this up: start by scanning kernel logs for "fallback" and run nsys around a confirmed p99 event (use the synthetic generator with zipf skew ~1.7). I can share the harness and config next week.

Signed-off: Arjun
